To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the permeability and release of ethinyl estradiol (EE), a contraceptive drug, from ethylene vinylacetate copolymer membrane and matrix, respectively, are dependent on the drug concentration in the donor solution, temperature, vinylacetate comonomer, and loading dose.
ethinylestradion release from EVA membrane is diffusion controlled and the drug release can be controlled by varying the membrane composition and thickness.

the drug permeability through EVA copolymeric membrane increased with an increased vinyl acetate content in the membrane, and the release of ethinyl estradiol from EVA membrane and EVA matrix was controlled by diffusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the membrane controlled drug delivery system for ethinylestradio.
the development of transdermal delivery of ethinyleestradiol using EVA copolyers.
the preparation of ethylene vinyl acetates membranes with different vinyl acetate comomomer contents and their permeability characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EVA membrane and matrix can be used as the drug delivery system for ethinylestradial.
ethinylestradial can be successfully delivered through the skin by the use of an EVA membrane.
the permeation of EE through EVA copolymeric membrane was diffusion controlled, and the drug release from the EVA matrix was diffusion controlled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the permeability coefficient of EE through EVA membrane is affected by the drug solubility in the donor solution and vinyl acetate comomonomer content of the EVA membrane.
the EVA copolyler membrane can be used as the matrix material to control the release rate of EE and PEG 400 can be used as a solubility enhancer to improve the drug permeability through the membrane.
the permeability of EE through EVA membrane is dependent on the vinyl acetate comomomer content in the copolymer, the thickness of membrane, drug concentration in the reservoir and the temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the release rates of the ethinylestradion from EVA matrix are controllable by changing the composition, temperature and loading doses.
the EVA copolymeric matrix is a promising candidate for the transdermal drug delivery system.
the release rate of EE can be controlled by varying the vinyl acetate content in EVA copolymeric membrane.
